items.description:
Affordable Office Factory Shop in Salt River specialises in used and second-hand office furniture for corporate and small businesses. The range covers office desks, chairs, cabinets and other office-related furniture, sourced to bring down the cost of fitting out a workspace.

Besides furnishing offices, the shop stocks stacker chairs, reception desks, sofas, canteen furniture, office accessories and a wide range of chairs. It suits businesses that want to furnish or refresh an office without paying new-furniture prices.

The shop is at 120 Voortrekker Road in Salt River, and it suits start-ups, growing businesses and anyone furnishing a reception, boardroom or canteen on a budget.

items.description:
AuTerra Jewellery is a jewellery studio at The Old Biscuit Mill in Woodstock, Cape Town. The studio handcrafts contemporary jewellery in gold and silver recycled from e-waste, working from its studio on site at the Mill.

The team believes in jewellery as something worth passing down, both as an heirloom object and as part of a more sustainable world for future generations to wear it in. Each piece is made with recycled precious metal rather than newly mined material.

The studio is open Monday to Saturday, and it suits shoppers who want handcrafted, sustainably made jewellery while browsing the Mill's market and design shops in Woodstock.

items.description:
The Bo-Kaap Museum is one of the earliest homes built in the Bo-Kaap, dating back to the mid-18th century, and it showcases local Islamic culture and heritage in the historic area that became home to many Muslims and freed slaves after the abolition of slavery. The house was declared a National Monument in 1965, restored in the 1970s, and established as a museum in 1978 as a satellite of the SA Cultural History Museum.

The museum is furnished as a house depicting the lifestyle of a nineteenth-century Cape Muslim family, and it is managed by Iziko Museums. Its facade has a curvilinear Baroque parapet typical of early Cape Dutch architecture, and a small courtyard behind it is reached by a narrow lane, paved in the Cape klip style.

The museum tells the story of the local community within a national social, political and cultural context, and it suits visitors who want to understand the history behind the colourful streets of the Bo-Kaap.

Bo-Vine Wine and Grill House is a seaside steak restaurant in Camps Bay, known for cooking what it calls the perfect steak. The grill runs a Steak Club, led by Pete Goffe-Wood and Steve Maresch, where members share steak experiences and get monthly recipes and recommendations on cuts for a Beef Box.

Steak Club members receive a welcome pack and draught beer, monthly deals on steak and braai items from Bo-Vine's online platform, invite-only events, and a 20% discount on the cut of the month. Joining is as simple as sending a name, email and cellphone number to the restaurant's events contact.

The restaurant is at Shop 1A, The Promenade on Victoria Road in Camps Bay, and it suits steak lovers and braai enthusiasts who want to go deeper than a single meal out.

items.description:
Cape Town Surfing is a surf school and surf store based in Hout Bay, operating since 2001 and describing itself as one of the oldest and most qualified surf schools in the area. It is a fully registered, insured school, and its instructors hold ISA and SSA Level 1 and 2 qualifications.

The business offers surf and SUP lessons and tours across Cape Town for all levels, from beginner groups and kids' clinics to advanced training, girls' surf groups, corporate team building and video analysis. Its store sells core surf, SUP and skate goods and offers board rentals, and it also runs sandboarding trips.

It works with SMTH Shapes, an established surfboard manufacturer known for premium quality boards. It suits beginners wanting their first lesson and experienced surfers looking for gear, tours or coaching in Hout Bay.

Car Smart Service Centre is an independent vehicle workshop in Ndabeni, founded in 2009 by Andrew Kendon and built around integrity, quality, good advice and fair value. The workshop is equipped with computerised diagnostic equipment and uses only leading brands of parts and consumables.

Every vehicle booked in for a service or repair gets a thorough, obligation-free examination and report on its condition, and clients are given a pre-quote for any necessary work before deciding whether to proceed. The team also disposes of workshop waste responsibly, and the centre is a registered and approved member of the Retail Motor Industry Organisation.

The business has built a loyal following, with customers who say they travel from across the city rather than compromise on service. It suits motorists who want honest diagnostics and transparent pricing in the Western Cape.

Cattle Baron Constantia is a steakhouse grill in the Constantia winelands, at Shop No 1, Old Constantia Village on Constantia Main Road. The revamped space has a spacious dining area, a vintage courtyard and a stylish bar, serving well-known steaks alongside a selection of local wines.

The restaurant charges no corkage fee on a first bottle brought in, and it has ample parking, which makes it convenient for both intimate dinners and light, casual lunches. The setting is described as combining true Cape hospitality with a warm, welcoming atmosphere for both visitors and locals.

It suits diners who want a relaxed steak dinner or lunch in a winelands setting, and quieter sittings are typically available on weekday afternoons.

Engel and Volkers Somerset West is a real estate agency at 171 Main Road, offering residential sales, investment properties, commercial space and luxury homes. Its agents work across Somerset West, Strand, Gordon's Bay and the Helderberg area, and services are offered in Afrikaans, English and German.

The branch is rated 4.5 out of five from 26 reviews, and it forms part of the wider Engel and Volkers network, which also helps clients find properties for rent and request a real estate appraisal. The agency offers both residential and commercial expertise under one roof.

It suits buyers, sellers and investors in the Helderberg area who want multilingual service and access to a global real estate brand's local office.

Feet4Life Lakeside is a podiatry branch at the Stone Village Wellness Centre on Main Road in Lakeside, part of a Cape Town practice that also has branches in Bellville, Constantia, Goodwood, Grassy Park, Mitchell's Plain and Rondebosch. The practice specialises in biomechanics, sports pathology and care for the diabetic foot.

Treatments cover ingrown toenails, fungal nails, calluses, corns, plantar warts, blisters, chilblains, athlete's foot, flat feet, heel pain, heel spurs, bunions and hammer or claw toes, along with wound care, orthotics and insoles, and footwear advice. Foot screenings are offered as a routine check for diabetic patients and for people with vascular or neurological symptoms.

The Lakeside branch works by appointment only and is a cashless practice, with medical aid accepted at selected branches. It suits patients who need specialist foot care close to Lakeside.

Finchley Guest House is a newly renovated guesthouse in the quiet heart of Camps Bay, a five-minute walk from the beach and the restaurants on the strip. It offers six en-suite bedrooms, each furnished in calming natural tones with air conditioning, internet TV, a fridge, a safe and a private bathroom.

Every sea-view room looks out across a 180-degree sweep of the Atlantic and the Twelve Apostles, and the guesthouse has been renovated to four-star standard aimed at guests visiting from Europe and further afield. There is a pool to relax by, and bookings can be made directly for the best value.

It suits couples and travellers who want a quiet, view-filled base within easy walking distance of Camps Bay beach.

Folk Cafe St James is a beach-style restaurant in St James, a newer sister branch of the popular Bree Street coffee and lunch spot in the city centre. The St James branch occupies the old Octopus Garden site and offers an all-new pizza and dinner menu, along with milkshakes and ice cream.

Co-owner Leeanne Heald describes it as a long-held dream to open a beach-style concept restaurant, and the site's beach vibe and large garden made room for a big kids' play area. The restaurant is run by Leeanne and her husband Laurence, who call it a beach-style concept store that is a little different from the original inner-city coffee shop.

It suits families who want pizza, dinner or ice cream with a beach-garden setting in St James.

Four Rosmead is a boutique luxury guest house on the slopes of Table Mountain in Oranjezicht, built in 1903 and recognised for its historical value. The building has been sensitively and stylishly remodelled, with chic, contemporary interiors carrying a subtle African spirit, enhanced by original South African artwork.

The guest house is within walking distance of Greenmarket Square and about ten minutes by car from the V&A Waterfront, Kirstenbosch Gardens, and the Clifton and Camps Bay beaches. It aims to offer the luxury and personal attention of a top-class boutique stay, suited to the discerning traveller or a romantic getaway.

It suits guests who want a historic, design-led guest house close to the city centre, with easy reach of Cape Town's beaches and gardens.

Grand Diamonds is a jewellery showroom in Green Point specialising in engagement rings, wedding bands and fine jewellery. Its Spring Summer 2026 collection includes eleven new natural diamond ring designs, ready to wear from the Cape Town showroom or customisable to order.

The range covers ladies' and men's wedding bands, bezel and claw pendants, signet rings, necklaces, bracelets and earrings, alongside an education hub covering diamond education and lab-grown diamonds. Customers can book a complimentary consultation to try on rings and discuss styles, diamond shapes and settings, or bring sketches and reference images to collaborate on a bespoke piece with the in-house jewellers.

It suits couples planning an engagement or wedding who want a ring designed and crafted specifically for them in Cape Town.

Grande Kloof Boutique Hotel is set in Cape Town's Fresnaye neighbourhood, offering two accommodation options under one roof. The Hotel Side is a four-star experience that includes breakfast, while the Apartment Side is a three-star, self-catering option suited to longer stays.

The property has sunny terraces, a pool area and a tranquil garden setting, with sea view, sea view deluxe and garden view rooms, as well as self-catering apartments. All units have air conditioning, and the hotel welcomes families and children of all ages. Shuttle services and airport pickups and drop-offs are available at an extra fee.

The hotel aims to make each guest feel valued, with personalised recommendations and warm hospitality from arrival to departure. It suits travellers who want either a full-service hotel stay or a self-catering base in a quiet part of the city.

items.description:
Heyns and Partners Inc is a law firm in Panorama offering commercial law, correspondent services, debt collection, divorce, insolvency law, labour law, litigation, notarial practice, personal injury, property law, and wills, trusts and estates. The firm describes its approach as fresh and innovative, built on solid legal foundations and aimed at efficient, quality service that suits each client's budget.

The firm is a member of Geneva Group International, a global alliance of independent firms, which gives it access to international legal expertise alongside local insight. Through this network the firm can draw on cross-border resources while still offering personalised, detail-oriented attention to each case.

It suits individuals and businesses who want a versatile legal team with both local knowledge and international reach.

Hoghouse Brewing Company is a brewery and barbecue restaurant in Ndabeni, an industrial suburb better known for light industry and office parks. The restaurant serves a Texan-style barbecue menu, braaiing items such as beef brisket, pork belly and lamb shoulder alongside its own beer.

The kitchen is headed by chef PJ Vadas, who has a fine-dining background that includes working with Gordon Ramsay in New York and heading two Eat Out Top 10 restaurants. At Hoghouse, he brings that experience to a more relaxed Southwestern-style barbecue offering, serving diners from nearby Pinelands and Maitland as well as further afield.

It suits barbecue fans who want a hearty, Texan-style meal with craft beer in an otherwise industrial part of Cape Town.

Indigo Brands is a cosmetics, fragrance and personal care manufacturer based in Epping Industria, Cape Town, and a wholly owned subsidiary of AVI Limited, which is listed on the JSE. The company has been creating, marketing, manufacturing and distributing cosmetics and toiletries from its Cape Town operations since 1955.

Its brands include Yardley, with ranges such as Bond St fragrance for him and her and English Blazer, and Lentheric, including Hoity Toity and the 48-hour protection range. The company says it is committed to providing products of the highest standard and continues to enhance its offerings while expanding beyond South Africa.

It suits retailers and consumers who buy long-established South African cosmetics and fragrance brands, and the company lists departments and vacancies for those interested in working with it.

items.description:
Kleinsky's Constantia is the southern suburbs branch of Sea Point's well-known bagel deli, now open at the High Constantia Centre. For more than a decade the Regent Road original built a loyal following on hand-rolled bagels, pastrami and what reviewers call some of the best rugelach in the city, a formula that led to further branches in Johannesburg and London.

The Constantia branch brings the same New York-style deli classics to Constantia, including bagels, breakfasts and other 'noshes'. A review in Time Out rated the branch four out of five stars, describing it as bringing Sea Point's bagel expertise to the leafy lanes of Constantia.

It suits deli fans in the southern suburbs who want New York-style bagels and breakfasts without travelling into the city.

Maharajah is an Indian restaurant group that began in 1979 on the idea of offering a meal worthy of its name at a modest price, using traditional Indian flavours and South African Indian cooking techniques. More than 40 years on, the restaurant is still run by the same family and still serves meals true to that heritage.

The group has two Cape Town locations: the original branch in Tamboerskloof, tucked below Table Mountain with a warm, vibrant dining room, and the newer Maharajah Eatery in the Rondebosch and Rosebank area, which offers a more laid-back, modern approach to the same menu. Reviewers praise the lamb curry on the bone and say the portions are generous enough to share.

It suits groups who want to share several dishes, and diners looking for a long-standing Cape Town Indian restaurant with a modern, relaxed branch nearby.

Morea House, Autograph Collection is a design-focused boutique hotel on Camps Bay Beach, with 90 rooms and suites, most offering mountain or ocean views. The hotel was brought to life by award-winning interior architect Tristan du Plessis, who used stone, timber and bronze tones to echo the sea, sand and mountains outside.

The lobby doubles as a gallery of South African art, showing work by artists including Chris Soal, WonderBuhle and Jeremy Rose, under a chandelier by Jan Ernst Studio shaped to mimic ocean wave flows. The hotel follows the Autograph Collection's philosophy of being exactly like nothing else, giving it a distinctive, one-of-a-kind character.

It suits travellers who want a design-led hotel on one of Cape Town's best-known beaches, with easy access to the promenade's restaurants and bars.

Our Local Sea Point is the second branch of the Kloof Street neighbourhood cafe that Michael Carter and Shayne Schutte built out of an old mechanic's workshop during lockdown. The Sea Point branch is smaller and more intimate than the original, but keeps the same long table down the centre and a window counter for watching the Sea Point buzz.

The cafe's eclectic style mixes plants, thrifted ceramics and salvaged furniture with rough-textured walls and vintage pieces, celebrating the beauty of imperfection rather than a polished finish. It serves an all-day menu of wholesome, home-style cooking in a relaxed, feel-good atmosphere suited to long breakfasts, lunches or catch-ups.

It suits visitors who want the same old-world, plant-filled charm as the original Our Local, in a more compact Sea Point setting.

items.description:
Rouge on Rose Boutique Hotel is a four-star hotel in the Bo-Kaap, which opened in 2008 with nine meticulously decorated suites. The historic neighbourhood is known for its colourful homes, the chanting from its mosques and its Malay community, and the hotel sits where cobblestone streets meet trendy bars, film studios and modelling agencies.

Rooms are available as deluxe suites or self-catering suites with a kitchenette, styled with the textures and design expected of luxury accommodation. The hotel is a short walk from the V&A Waterfront, the Cape Town International Convention Centre, Bree and Kloof Streets, De Waterkant, and a cluster of fine dining restaurants, art galleries and museums, and only a quick drive from Table Mountain, Camps Bay and the Constantia Wine Route.

It suits holiday and business travellers who want a centrally located, design-focused stay in one of Cape Town's most distinctive neighbourhoods.

Rummage Preloved is a vintage and second-hand clothing store in the courtyard of Imhoff Farm in Kommetjie, run by two friends, Zelda Bate and Tracey Nevill, who met through their children's school on the farm. The shop sells a curated selection of one-off pieces, chosen for quality and style, each one sourced, laundered, pressed and priced with care.

Alongside the rails of clothing, the shop holds a range of accessories, and it accepts clothing on consignment, encouraging customers to sell old pieces and buy second-hand rather than add to the waste of the clothing industry. The two owners enjoy matching vintage treasures to the customers who will appreciate them.

It suits shoppers looking for a summer frock, winter woollens or a special-occasion outfit with a story, rather than something off a factory rail.

items.description:
The Salty Sea Dog is a fish and chips restaurant on Wharf Street in Simon's Town, with views over the harbour and the Southern Apostles mountains. The restaurant describes its signature hake, pulled straight from the sea onto the plate, as the dish that defines it, prepared with a variety of choices in an inviting, fully licensed setting.

Run by Penny and Joe, the restaurant aims to keep things uncomplicated, affordable and true to the spirit of the coast, with both a sit-down menu and a take-away menu. Local landmarks and the walk down into Wharf Street are part of the experience of finding the restaurant.

It suits visitors to Simon's Town who want fresh fish and chips with harbour views, whether sitting down or taking away.

Siki's Koffee Kafe is a coffee shop in Khayelitsha, launched in 2016 by Sikelela 'Siki' Dibela after nine years working in the coffee industry, starting out washing dishes at a Vida e Caffe branch. The cafe operates from a garage at his mother's house and has grown into a busy, vibey hub attracting entrepreneurs, students and locals alike.

The cafe draws entrepreneurs, students, police officials and community members from across the area, and its customers have included Springbok captain Siya Kolisi. Dibela went on to supervise the opening of a coffee shop in London before returning to open his own cafe in the township.

It suits coffee lovers who want a genuine township coffee culture experience in Khayelitsha, built from one barista's own journey through the industry.

items.description:
Spec-Savers Richmond Corner is an optometry store at Shop 15, Richmond Corner, on the corner of Tygerberg Valley and Plattekloof Roads in Milnerton. The branch offers eye examinations, contact lens fittings, driver's licence screenings and a range of spectacles, sunglasses and contact lenses, along with gift cards and lens customisation.

The practice describes its approach as combining professional standards with quality eyewear at affordable prices, and customers can book an eye test directly with the branch. Spec-Savers is part of a group of stores across South Africa, Namibia, Botswana, Lesotho and Swaziland, and is a member of the MediWallet medical account network.

It suits people in the Milnerton area who want an eye test, new glasses or a driver's licence screening close to home.

Spec-Savers Bothasig is an optometry store at Shop 7, Bothasig Mall, on the corner of Vryburger Avenue and Tafelberg Street. The branch offers eye examinations and sells spectacles, sunglasses and contact lenses, along with gift cards and a range of lens types and coatings.

The store describes its staff as friendly and well trained, aiming to combine professional optometric standards with a wide selection of frames at affordable prices. Spec-Savers is part of a group of stores across South Africa, Namibia, Botswana, Lesotho and Swaziland, and also offers an audiology service for hearing care.

It suits residents of Bothasig and the surrounding suburbs who want an eye test or new glasses close to the mall.

Tambourine is a modern small-plates restaurant in District Six, built around a farm-to-fork approach that starts with pasture-raised beef, lamb and chicken and vegetables grown mostly on its own pesticide-free, regenerative farm project in Khayelitsha. Fish is line-caught and wild whenever possible, and the kitchen works only with family-run, traceable dairy.

Every dish is crafted from scratch, including the bread and pasta, and the kitchen cooks over open fire while sticking to what is local, seasonal and organic. Even food waste is composted back into the soil that grows the next harvest, so the restaurant describes every plate as telling a story that starts with care.

The restaurant is at 104 Harrington Street in District Six, and it suits diners who want a considered, farm-to-table meal built on small plates.

The Bay Hotel is a luxury beachfront hotel in Camps Bay, with the Atlantic Ocean on its doorstep and the Twelve Apostles mountain range as a backdrop. Its in-house breakfast restaurant, Tides, serves a South African breakfast buffet with views over the beachfront strip, while Bistro at The Bay suits a glass of wine and a leisurely lunch.

Guests can relax at the hotel's private beach club, Sandy B, or at Caamil's Bar while watching the sunset. The hotel has four swimming pools, a gym, indoor and outdoor padel courts and a spa, and it offers pet-friendly accommodation for guests who do not want to leave a pet behind.

It suits business travellers, couples and families who want a beachfront stay with dining, wellness and padel all on site in Camps Bay.

items.description:
The Little Fisherman is a fish shop in Lakeside, Cape Town, describing itself as a purveyor of fine fish. It stocks fresh oysters and crayfish in season, along with daily fresh catches sourced from sustainable suppliers, and a wide range of imported products and accompaniments.

Recent catches advertised by the shop have included fresh yellowtail straight from Cape Point, hot smoked salmon and bluefin tuna, alongside prawns prepared to order. The shop also shares guidance on its range, such as a World Oyster Selection Guide comparing different oyster varieties by shell shape, size, texture and growing environment.

The shop is at the Old Bakery on the corner of Main and Lincoln Roads in Lakeside, and it suits home cooks and seafood lovers who want fresh, sustainably sourced fish and shellfish.

items.description:
Virgin Active Steenberg is a gym with a heated lap pool for lane swimming and squad training, plus a smaller heated leisure pool for aqua classes, swimming lessons or play. The club has a sauna and steam room, functional training equipment such as kettlebells, Bulgarian bags and slam balls, a Ride studio for indoor cycling, and a Mind Body studio for yoga and Pilates.

Other facilities include a rowing area, Wattbikes with app integration, an access-controlled kids' space called Club V for children from six weeks to 13 years, an accessible changeroom, treatment rooms for massage therapists and physiotherapists, and free WiFi. Membership pricing varies by age and contract length, and the club offers a free gym plan trial and a refer-a-friend scheme.

It suits families and serious trainers alike who want a full-service gym with pools, classes and childcare in Steenberg.
